title: Epidemic Sound Pricing: Plans and Costs (2026 Guide)
summary: Epidemic sound pricing ranges from $119.88 to $360 annually across Creator, Pro and Business tiers. Understand which plan matches your publishing needs.
body_markdown:
## The Strongest Case Against Paying for Epidemic Sound


A subscription is rent, you own nothing when you stop paying, and free or per-track libraries cover much of what a small channel needs.


### The objection at full strength


If you don't use the thing constantly, rent makes no sense. Epidemic Sound's Creator plan is $119.88 a year, which is $9.99 a month whether you publish or not, so the per-video cost depends entirely on your output.


In a quiet month, a free library costs nothing, and a single-track licence costs money only in the month you buy one. For a creator who's still finding a format, that's a real argument.


### When Epidemic Sound costs too much per video


Here is what the objection costs the occasional publisher, per the[Epidemic Sound pricing page](https://www.epidemicsound.com/pricing/) : at one video a month, Creator works out to $9.99 per video.


That's more than a $5 or $8 single-track licence and close to a $12 one, so you're paying a premium for access you barely touch.


If you post once a month, or in bursts, buy per track or use free music. The subscription loses.


### Why the subscription still holds for regular publishers


It doesn't grow with volume. At 10 videos a month the same plan costs $0.999 per video, so the price per upload has fallen to about a dollar.


At 30 videos a month it's $0.333 per video, a third of a dollar for music that carries a commercial licence.


Creator is a flat $119.88 line, set against single-track licences at $5, $8 and $12 each.


Read the crossing points: at $12 a track, Creator is cheaper from the 10th track in a year. At $8 it's cheaper from the 15th, and at $5 from the 24th.


A channel publishing weekly with one track per video uses about **52 tracks a year** , so even the cheapest per-track price ($5) comes to $260, **more than double the subscription** .


Under roughly one to two videos a month, the objection wins. Above that, rent's the cheaper way to hold the licence.
